class.name: ECSScheduler
class.brief_description: The execution engine that drives the ECS simulation lifecycle.
class.description: [ECSScheduler] is the orchestrator responsible for executing simulation systems in a deterministic and high-performance manner. It integrates deeply with Godot's [NOTIFICATION_PROCESS] and [NOTIFICATION_PHYSICS_PROCESS] to ensure that ECS logic runs in sync with the rest of the engine. The scheduler manages both [b]Native Systems[/b] (hard-coded C++ systems like Physics, Rendering, and Hierarchy) and [b]Scripting Systems[/b] (GDScript [Callable]s). It utilizes a dependency-aware execution model, allowing systems to run in parallel on the [WorkerThreadPool] if they do not share writing access to the same component types. [b]Note:[/b] The order of execution is critical. Native systems generally run first to prepare the frame state, followed by user-defined systems, and finally structural cleanup via the [ECSCommandBuffer]. Through the [method get_detailed_stats] and [method get_system_timings] methods, developers can profile the simulation in real-time, identifying bottlenecks down to individual microsecond timings for every registered system.

method.name: register_process_system
method.description: Adds a system to the [b]Process[/b] queue. This system will be executed every frame during Godot's main idle processing. Ideal for logic that requires high-frequency visual updates (e.g., camera following, aesthetic animations).

method.name: register_physics_system
method.description: Adds a system to the [b]Physics[/b] queue. This system will be executed during the fixed physics tick, ensuring deterministic results regardless of frame rate. Ideal for movement, collision handling, and AI sensors.

method.name: set_system_enabled
method.description: Toggles the execution state of a specific system. Disabled systems remain in the registry but are skipped during the simulation pass. This is useful for pausing specific gameplay mechanics or optimizing performance in low-activity zones.

method.name: is_system_enabled
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the provided system is currently active in the execution queue.

method.name: get_system_timings
method.description: Returns a collection of timing data for all registered systems. The keys are system names (or Callable descriptions) and the values are execution durations in microseconds from the last frame.

method.name: register_system_dependency
method.description: Defines the "Archetype Interest" of a system. The [param read_mask] and [param write_mask] are bitfields representing the component types the system accesses. Use the [code]BIT_*[/code] constants from [EntityManager] to build these masks (e.g., [code]EntityManager.BIT_TRANSFORM | EntityManager.BIT_PHYSICS_3D[/code]). The [ECSScheduler] uses this information to detect race conditions and automatically parallelize systems that operate on distinct data sets. If two systems share a write bit, they will be forced to run sequentially.

method.name: get_detailed_stats
method.description: Returns a comprehensive telemetry report including frame budget usage, entity population spikes, and multi-thread contention metrics.

method.name: validate_simulation_integrity
method.description: Audits the internal schedule to detect logical errors such as write-write conflicts or circular system dependencies.
